clue.text: Punishments or signs of love?

definitions.meaning: slaps on the bottom given to a naughty child
loud kisses, the noisy kind planted on a cheek

explanation.surface: A wry question: are spankings really a form of affection?
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both blows with the open hand and hearty, audible kisses.

clue.text: Winner such as Bob at Aintree in 1981? …

definitions.text: such as Bob at Aintree in 1981?
definitions.meaning: the jockey Bob who rode Aldaniti to victory in the 1981 Grand National at Aintree, after beating cancer

explanation.surface: Recalls a famous racing victory at Aintree, the Liverpool course that hosts the Grand National steeplechase.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 3-down, whose clue is in the voice of another famous winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A title-holder or victor is the general sense; the second is the surname of jockey Bob, the 1981 Grand National hero.

clue.text: … or maybe me at Wimbledon in 1975, in a rush, heart fluttering?

definitions.text: … or maybe me at Wimbledon in 1975

indicators.note: a heart that flutters beats irregularly, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tennis player recalls the nervous excitement of winning Wimbledon in 1975.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues 2-down: another winner, this time speaking as 'me'. 'fluttering' shuffles RUSH HEART into RTHURASHE, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: The American tennis star beat Jimmy Connors in the 1975 Wimbledon men's singles final, a famous upset victory.

clue.text: Artist, good person set up as policy chief

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are raised, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good person

explanation.surface: A painter and a decent sort promoted to head of policy in some organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses RAST in this down entry. A 'tsar' is journalese for a government-appointed head of some policy area, such as a drugs tsar.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers call officials appointed to lead a policy area, like a drugs or energy supremo, by the old Russian imperial title.

clue.text: Person to tell what you're thinking as one entering pit full of fear

definitions.text: Person to tell what you're thinking

indicators.note: the pit-worker is filled with the fear, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a miner goes down a pit, a coal mine
dread is great fear

explanation.surface: A coal worker going down a pit, terrified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one entering pit' looks like part of the definition's picture, but it is the pit-worker who holds the fear; 'full of' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A telepath or psychic performer claims to know other people's thoughts.

clue.text: Member of family, 23, participated in marathon maybe

parts.note: 23-across's answer is the spoken name of the seventh letter of the alphabet, so it stands for that letter
a marathon is a long race, so taking part means one ran

explanation.surface: A relative who took part in a marathon run.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 23 gives the letter G, since 23-across spells out how that letter is said.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandmother, informally shortened, is a relative in the family.

clue.text: Item of clothes that is on fire?

definitions.meaning: a jacket, often with a school or club badge
something burning fiercely, which is ablaze

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a garment going up in flames.
explanation.definitionFit: The jacket is named from the bright red coats of a Cambridge rowing club; literally, a thing ablaze.

clue.text: Plant in a container in the manner indicated

parts.note: a can is a tin container
thus means in this way, as shown

explanation.surface: Instructions to pot a plant in a container as shown.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean plant with spiny leaves, whose leaf shape decorates Corinthian column capitals.

clue.text: Mike has hair styled by one wise man

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: hair that is styled is rearranged, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Mike gets his hair done by somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'styled' is the anagram signal; 'by' just places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu guru or spiritual teacher, a title meaning 'great sage', as with the Beatles' guru.

clue.text: Holy bones maybe Roman Catholic priest collected

indicators.note: the church abbreviation has gathered the priest in, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: Saints' bones gathered up by a Catholic priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' signals the container; Eli is the biblical priest who raised the boy Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A saint's bones or belongings kept for veneration are an example of a revered remnant.

clue.text: Oil in river by house at edge of settlement

indicators.note: the house with the river sits right after the settlement, at its edge
the river comes next to the house

parts.note: a camp is a temporary settlement

explanation.surface: Oil found in a river beside a house on the outskirts of a village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil in river' tempts a solver to put something inside a river; 'in' is only a link, and 'by' and 'at edge of' set the pieces end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong-smelling aromatic substance, taken from a tree, that is used in oils and ointments.

clue.text: Resident of French province sent to religious school

parts.note: de is French for 'of'
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: Someone from a French region is packed off to a religious school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resident of French province' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Resident'. Northern Ireland is called 'the Province' in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhabitant, someone who dwells in a particular place.

clue.text: Slide involving some riskiness

indicators.note: the answer takes in some of the letters of the next word, lying within it

explanation.surface: A slip that involves some danger.
explanation.definitionFit: To glide over snow on runners, a kind of sliding.

clue.text: What may excite Mrs: heron may in part of Kent

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wading bird might thrill a lady birdwatcher in a corner of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excite' stirs MRS HERON MAY into the place name. It is a marshland area of south-east England, in Kent, good for birdwatching.
explanation.definitionFit: This wetland stretch of the Kent coast, famed for its sheep, lies in the south-east of that county.

clue.text: Maiden, one French friend wanting to be a companion somewhere in Florida

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
I is the Roman numeral one
ami is French for friend
taken as written
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A young woman and her French friend want to become companions.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored. CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort city on a barrier island near the city it is named after, in that south-eastern US state.

clue.text: Easy for one?

parts.note: Easy is the title hero of Captain Marryat's 1836 naval novel, a young officer-in-training at sea

explanation.surface: Reads like a remark that a task is simple for a single person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easy' looks like an adjective but is a character's surname, from Marryat's novel about a young naval cadet.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Easy, Marryat's hero, holds the junior naval rank of an officer cadet, so he is an example.

clue.text: Entertains with rhyme

parts.note: a rhyming phrase meaning to host guests lavishly over food, drink

explanation.surface: Reads as amusing people with verses.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme is not verse recited to guests; it describes the phrase itself, whose two halves rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat someone generously with a meal plus drink is to host lavishly, a rhyming idiom.

clue.text: A crew with keg at sea that may be afloat after accident

definitions.text: that may be afloat after accident

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailing crew with a barrel adrift after a shipwreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' fits the nautical picture but signals the anagram of A CREW KEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating debris and broken remains are what is left after a crash or shipwreck.

clue.text: See 17
See 17
A sort of image, no?

definitions.meaning: a photographic film image with light and dark reversed
a refusal or denial, as an answer

explanation.surface: A tentative question about whether a picture is of some kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Film photographs produce inverted-tone images; the word also means a refusal or 'no'.

clue.text: Northern town with one cunning old church ruler

parts.note: Eccles is a town near Manchester, in northern England, home of the Eccles cake
I is the Roman numeral one
arch means sly or knowing

explanation.surface: A sly character from a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccles is a town near Manchester, famous for its currant cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical title for a ruler or prelate of a church, from the Greek for assembly plus chief.

clue.text: Washes cold meat — first requirement for safety

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
lean is meat without fat

indicators.note: the first thing needed for the next word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Hygiene advice: washing cold meat is the first rule of food safety.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub or launder something is to wash it.

clue.text: Only one half of the pantomime animal? Goodness!

indicators.note: a pantomime horse is two actors, one in each half; we take half the word

parts.note: a horse, the stage costume worked by two actors, here in its doubled nursery-talk name

explanation.surface: A pantomime horse is played by two actors, front and back, so each is half the animal.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime horse, a British Christmas stage costume, is worked by two people. 'Only one half of' halves the nursery word for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of surprise, like 'Gosh!' or 'Wow!'

clue.text: Listen, stupid recruit!

indicators.note: a stupid arrangement is a senseless one, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant barking at a dim new soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recruit' looks like the noun being shouted at, but the definition is the verb: sign up.
explanation.definitionFit: To join up or sign on, especially for the armed forces, is to become a recruit.

clue.text: King, the fellow to go down with viceroy

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess
he refers to a man
to dive is to plunge downwards

explanation.surface: A king and his man sink along with a viceroy.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the Ottoman governor, effectively a viceroy, who ruled Egypt.

clue.text: Have a desire to reside in Whitchurch

indicators.note: the answer lives inside the place name that follows, as a hidden run of letters

explanation.surface: Someone longing to live in Whitchurch, a small market town in Shropshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn or long for something is to be restless with craving.

clue.text: What business needs to get going in London?

definitions.text: What business needs to get going
definitions.meaning: the money invested to start an enterprise
the chief city of the United Kingdom, seat of government

explanation.surface: A question about what funding a London start-up requires.
explanation.definitionFit: Funds for investment are one sense; London is the seat of the UK government, an example of the other.

clue.text: Banks contain all your savings? Only bits of them

indicators.note: just a bit of each of these words is used, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A cynic asks whether banks really hold your money, or only some of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' looks financial but means sandbanks or reefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Low islands or sandbanks of coral, as in the Florida Keys, are banks in the geographical sense.

clue.text: Officer in charge of biological unit

parts.note: GEN is the abbreviation for general, a senior officer

explanation.surface: Describes the officer running a unit of soldiers studying biology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unit' suggests a military unit, but the definition is 'of biological unit', an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective meaning relating to genes, the basic hereditary units of biology.

clue.text: What rival claimants to baby wouldn't do for Solomon — wailing diminishes

definitions.text: What rival claimants to baby wouldn't do for Solomon

parts.note: to wail is to cry
halves means cuts in two, reduces

explanation.surface: Solomon's judgment: two women claim one baby, and the true mother wails at his plan to divide it.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible, Solomon offered to cut the disputed baby in two; the real mother refused to claim an equal share.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to claim an equal share, which the true mother would never accept for her child.
